config.title: Heartland Road Atlas
config.subtitle: Museums, architecture, Americana and parks in seven states, with driving times from Champaign, IL
config.guideIntro: Trip regions grouped by typical driving time from Champaign, so you can match a guide to the time you have: a day trip, an overnight or a long weekend. Driving times come from OpenStreetMap routing without traffic, so allow extra time for stops and city driving.

sites.name: Krannert Art Museum
sites.desc: The University of Illinois art museum, free to all, with ancient Andean ceramics, African art, European paintings and contemporary work.

sites.name: Spurlock Museum of World Cultures
sites.desc: University museum of world cultures with galleries on Mesopotamia, Egypt, Europe, the Americas, Africa and Asia.

sites.name: Krannert Center for the Performing Arts
sites.desc: Max Abramovitz's 1969 complex of four theaters around a grand brick lobby, one of the major performing arts centers of the Midwest.
sites.wiki: Krannert Center for the Performing Arts

sites.name: Museum of the Grand Prairie
sites.desc: Champaign County Forest Preserve museum in Mahomet on prairie life, Lincoln's circuit-riding years and local history.

sites.name: Robert Allerton Park
sites.desc: Robert Allerton's estate on the Sangamon River, given to the University of Illinois in 1946: formal gardens, the Fu Dog Garden and the Sun Singer within woods and prairie.

sites.name: Kickapoo State Recreation Area
sites.desc: Former strip-mine land regrown into forest and ponds on the Middle Fork of the Vermilion, Illinois's only National Wild and Scenic River.

sites.name: Lincoln Log Cabin State Historic Site
sites.desc: The farm of Thomas and Sarah Bush Lincoln, run as a living history farm of the 1840s near Charleston.
sites.wiki: Lincoln Log Cabin State Historic Site

sites.name: Big Things Small Town, Casey
sites.desc: A small town that turned itself into a roadside attraction with a dozen record-setting giant objects, from a wind chime to a mailbox.

sites.name: Arthur and Illinois Amish Country
sites.desc: The center of the largest Amish settlement in Illinois, with farm shops, bakeries and buggies on the county roads.

sites.name: David Davis Mansion
sites.desc: The 1872 Italianate villa of Lincoln's friend and Supreme Court justice David Davis in Bloomington, a state historic site.

sites.name: McLean County Museum of History
sites.desc: A regional history museum in the domed 1903 courthouse on Bloomington's square.

sites.name: Abraham Lincoln Presidential Library and Museum
sites.desc: Immersive galleries on Lincoln's life and a major research library of Lincoln and Illinois history, opened in 2005.
sites.wiki: Abraham Lincoln Presidential Library and Museum

sites.name: Lincoln Home National Historic Site
sites.desc: The only home Lincoln owned, where he lived from 1844 to 1861, in a restored four-block neighborhood.

sites.name: Dana-Thomas House
sites.desc: Frank Lloyd Wright's Prairie house for Susan Lawrence Dana (1902 to 1904), with its original art glass and furniture.

sites.name: Lincoln Tomb
sites.desc: Burial place of Abraham Lincoln, Mary Lincoln and three of their sons in Oak Ridge Cemetery.

sites.name: Old State Capitol
sites.desc: The Greek Revival capitol where Lincoln gave the House Divided speech in 1858.
sites.wiki: Old State Capitol State Historic Site

sites.name: Illinois State Capitol
sites.desc: The domed capitol completed in 1888, with free tours of its decorated chambers.

sites.name: Illinois State Museum
sites.desc: Natural history, archaeology and art of Illinois, from mastodons to Native American life and Illinois artists.

sites.name: Lincoln's New Salem
sites.desc: Reconstruction of the village where young Lincoln lived from 1831 to 1837.

sites.name: Cozy Dog Drive In
sites.desc: Route 66 diner in Springfield that claims the invention of the corn dog on a stick.

sites.name: Illinois Route 66 Hall of Fame and Museum
sites.desc: A Route 66 museum in Pontiac, surrounded by murals and memorabilia of the old highway.

sites.name: Funks Grove Pure Maple Sirup
sites.desc: Family maple syrup farm on old Route 66 near Shirley, still spelling sirup the old way.
sites.wiki: Funk's Grove Township, McLean County, Illinois

sites.name: Gemini Giant
sites.desc: A 1960s fiberglass Muffler Man astronaut standing on Route 66 in Wilmington.

sites.name: Midewin National Tallgrass Prairie
sites.desc: Restored tallgrass prairie on a former army arsenal near Wilmington, grazed by a bison herd.

sites.name: Starved Rock State Park
sites.desc: Sandstone canyons on the Illinois River with spring waterfalls, winter bald eagles and a 1930s CCC lodge.

sites.name: Matthiessen State Park
sites.desc: A quieter neighbor of Starved Rock with a deep dells canyon, stone bridges and falls.

sites.name: Peoria Riverfront Museum
sites.desc: Art, history and science museum with a planetarium on the Peoria riverfront.

sites.name: Wildlife Prairie Park
sites.desc: Park near Peoria with bison, elk, wolves and other native animals of Illinois in large habitats.

sites.name: Farnsworth House
sites.desc: Mies van der Rohe's glass house on the Fox River at Plano (1951), a defining work of modern domestic architecture.

sites.name: Illinois Railway Museum
sites.desc: One of the largest railway museums in the country, at Union, with operating trains on summer weekends.

sites.name: Laurent House
sites.desc: Frank Lloyd Wright's Usonian house in Rockford for Kenneth Laurent, a wheelchair user, and an early example of accessible design.

sites.name: Anderson Japanese Gardens
sites.desc: A celebrated Japanese garden in Rockford with ponds, waterfalls and a tea house.

sites.name: Burpee Museum of Natural History
sites.desc: Rockford museum best known for Jane, a juvenile Tyrannosaurus skeleton.

sites.name: Ronald Reagan Boyhood Home
sites.desc: The Dixon house where Reagan lived as a boy in the 1920s.

sites.name: John Deere Historic Site
sites.desc: Grand Detour, where John Deere built his self-scouring steel plow in 1837, with a working blacksmith shop.

sites.name: Galena Historic District
sites.desc: A 19th-century lead-mining boomtown of brick commercial streets in the hills above the Galena River.

sites.name: Ulysses S. Grant Home
sites.desc: The house Galena's citizens gave Grant on his return from the Civil War in 1865.

sites.name: Mississippi Palisades State Park
sites.desc: Limestone bluffs and overlooks above the Mississippi near Savanna.

sites.name: Bishop Hill
sites.desc: A Swedish Pietist colony founded in 1846, preserved as a village of colony buildings and museums.

sites.name: Black Hawk State Historic Site
sites.desc: Wooded bluffs in Rock Island with a museum of the Sauk and Meskwaki nations.

sites.name: Nauvoo Historic District
sites.desc: Mississippi River town built by Latter-day Saints from 1839 to 1846, with many restored houses and shops.

sites.name: Pere Marquette State Park
sites.desc: Bluffs at the meeting of the Illinois and Mississippi rivers, a CCC stone lodge and winter eagle watching.

sites.name: Elsah
sites.desc: A tiny 19th-century stone village tucked into a hollow of the Great River Road, entirely on the National Register.

sites.name: National Great Rivers Museum
sites.desc: Corps of Engineers museum at the Mel Price Locks and Dam, with lock tours.

sites.name: Lewis and Clark State Historic Site
sites.desc: Camp River Dubois, where the Corps of Discovery wintered in 1803 to 1804 before heading west.
sites.wiki: Lewis and Clark State Historic Site

sites.name: Cahokia Mounds
sites.desc: The largest pre-Columbian city north of Mexico, centered on Monks Mound. A UNESCO World Heritage Site.

sites.name: Chain of Rocks Bridge
sites.desc: The old Route 66 bridge over the Mississippi with its famous 22 degree bend, now open to walkers and cyclists.

sites.name: World's Largest Catsup Bottle
sites.desc: A 1949 water tower in Collinsville shaped like a giant catsup bottle.

sites.name: Garden of the Gods
sites.region: Southern Illinois and the Lower Ohio
sites.desc: Wind-carved sandstone formations in the Shawnee National Forest with wide views over the hills.

sites.name: Giant City State Park
sites.region: Southern Illinois and the Lower Ohio
sites.desc: Sandstone streets of giant bluffs and a CCC lodge near Carbondale.

sites.name: Cache River State Natural Area
sites.region: Southern Illinois and the Lower Ohio
sites.desc: Cypress and tupelo swamps, with some of the oldest trees east of the Mississippi.

sites.name: Cave-In-Rock State Park
sites.region: Southern Illinois and the Lower Ohio
sites.desc: A river cave on the Ohio once used by outlaws and river pirates.

sites.name: Superman statue, Metropolis
sites.region: Southern Illinois and the Lower Ohio
sites.desc: Metropolis embraces its name with a 15 foot Superman statue on the courthouse square.

sites.name: Fort de Chartres
sites.region: Southern Illinois and the Lower Ohio
sites.desc: A reconstructed 18th-century French stone fort in the American Bottom.

sites.name: Columbus modernist downtown
sites.desc: A small city where the Cummins Foundation paid architects' fees for public buildings by the Saarinens, I. M. Pei, Harry Weese and others. Tours leave from the visitors center.

sites.name: First Christian Church, Columbus
sites.desc: Eliel Saarinen's 1942 church, one of the first modern churches in America.

sites.name: North Christian Church
sites.desc: Eero Saarinen's last building (1964), a hexagon under a soaring spire.

sites.name: Miller House and Garden
sites.desc: Eero Saarinen's 1957 house for J. Irwin Miller, with interiors by Alexander Girard and a garden by Dan Kiley. Tours by reservation.

sites.name: Eskenazi Museum of Art
sites.desc: Indiana University's art museum in I. M. Pei's triangular building, with strong African, ancient and modern collections.

sites.name: Lilly Library
sites.desc: Indiana University's rare book library, with a Gutenberg Bible New Testament and changing exhibitions.

sites.name: Brown County State Park
sites.desc: Indiana's largest state park, forested hills at their best in October, near the art colony town of Nashville.

sites.name: T. C. Steele State Historic Site
sites.desc: Home, studio and gardens of the Hoosier Group painter Theodore Clement Steele.
sites.wiki: T. C. Steele State Historic Site

sites.name: McCormick's Creek State Park
sites.desc: Indiana's first state park, with a limestone canyon and waterfall.

sites.name: Newfields (Indianapolis Museum of Art)
sites.desc: A large encyclopedic art museum with gardens, the Lilly House and the 100 Acres art and nature park.

sites.name: The Children's Museum of Indianapolis
sites.desc: Often called the world's largest children's museum, with dinosaurs, a carousel and science galleries.

sites.name: Eiteljorg Museum
sites.desc: Native American and Western art in White River State Park.
sites.wiki: Eiteljorg Museum of American Indians and Western Art

sites.name: Indiana State Museum
sites.desc: State museum of science, culture and history on the canal in White River State Park.

sites.name: Kurt Vonnegut Museum and Library
sites.desc: A small museum devoted to the Indianapolis-born novelist.

sites.name: Indianapolis Motor Speedway Museum
sites.desc: Race cars and history at the track of the Indianapolis 500.

sites.name: Indiana World War Memorial
sites.desc: A five-block civic plaza with a monumental memorial and military museum, modeled on the Mausoleum of Halicarnassus.

sites.name: Scottish Rite Cathedral
sites.desc: A Tudor Gothic Masonic hall of 1929 with a carillon tower, open for tours.

sites.name: Soldiers' and Sailors' Monument
sites.desc: The neoclassical monument at the center of Monument Circle, with an observation deck.

sites.name: Benjamin Harrison Presidential Site
sites.desc: The Italianate home of the 23rd president.

sites.name: Indiana Medical History Museum
sites.desc: The preserved 1896 pathology building of Central State Hospital.

sites.name: Crown Hill Cemetery
sites.desc: One of the largest cemeteries in the country, a landscaped park with John Dillinger's grave and a city view from the Crown.

sites.name: Conner Prairie
sites.desc: Living history museum in Fishers recreating Indiana life in the 1830s.

sites.name: David Owsley Museum of Art
sites.desc: Ball State University's art museum, with a broad collection from antiquity to contemporary art in a 1936 building.

sites.name: Minnetrista
sites.desc: Museum and gardens on the former estates of the Ball brothers, makers of the Ball canning jar.

sites.name: Richmond Art Museum
sites.desc: American Impressionist and Hoosier Group paintings, housed inside a working high school.

sites.name: Gennett Records Walk of Fame
sites.desc: Richmond's tribute to the studio where Louis Armstrong, Jelly Roll Morton and Hoagy Carmichael made early jazz records.

sites.name: Levi and Catharine Coffin House
sites.desc: Fountain City home of Quaker abolitionists known as a station on the Underground Railroad.

sites.name: Turkey Run State Park
sites.desc: Sandstone ravines and ladders along Sugar Creek, among the most rugged hiking in Indiana.

sites.name: Shades State Park
sites.desc: Quieter sandstone canyons and overlooks above Sugar Creek.

sites.name: Parke County covered bridges
sites.desc: More than 30 historic covered bridges around Rockville, with a large festival every October.

sites.name: Swope Art Museum
sites.desc: American art in an Art Deco interior in downtown Terre Haute, free.

sites.name: Tippecanoe Battlefield
sites.desc: Site of the 1811 battle near Lafayette, with a museum and a monument.

sites.name: Grissom Air Museum
sites.desc: Military aircraft displayed outdoors next to Grissom Air Reserve Base.

sites.name: New Harmony
sites.desc: Town of two 19th-century utopian experiments, with Philip Johnson's Roofless Church and Richard Meier's Atheneum.

sites.name: Lincoln Boyhood National Memorial
sites.desc: The farm where Lincoln lived from age 7 to 21 and the grave of his mother, Nancy Hanks Lincoln.

sites.name: West Baden Springs Hotel
sites.desc: A 1902 resort hotel whose atrium dome was long called the largest free-spanning dome in the world.

sites.name: George Rogers Clark National Historical Park
sites.desc: A circular classical memorial on the Wabash in Vincennes, built 1931 to 1933.
sites.wiki: George Rogers Clark National Historical Park

sites.name: Angel Mounds
sites.desc: A Mississippian town site on the Ohio near Evansville with large earthen mounds.

sites.name: Spring Mill State Park
sites.desc: Caves, old-growth forest and a restored pioneer village with a working gristmill.

sites.name: Marengo Cave
sites.desc: A show cave discovered in 1883, among the most visited in the Midwest.

sites.name: Holiday World
sites.desc: A family amusement park in the town of Santa Claus, known for its wooden roller coasters.

sites.name: Indiana Dunes National Park
sites.desc: Dunes, beaches, bogs and oak savanna on the Lake Michigan shore, the birthplace of plant ecology research.

sites.name: Studebaker National Museum
sites.desc: Wagons, carriages and cars built by Studebaker in South Bend.

sites.name: Raclin Murphy Museum of Art
sites.desc: The University of Notre Dame's new art museum, opened in 2023 at the campus gateway.

sites.name: Basilica of the Sacred Heart
sites.desc: A Gothic Revival church on the Notre Dame campus with murals by Luigi Gregori.
sites.wiki: Basilica of the Sacred Heart (Notre Dame)

sites.name: RV/MH Hall of Fame
sites.desc: Elkhart museum of vintage campers and travel trailers in the capital of the RV industry.

sites.name: Shipshewana
sites.desc: Amish town known for its flea market, auctions and the Menno-Hof heritage center.

sites.name: Auburn Cord Duesenberg Automobile Museum
sites.desc: Classic cars displayed in the company's 1930 Art Deco showroom and headquarters.

sites.name: Fort Wayne Museum of Art
sites.desc: American art from the 19th century to today, with a strong print and glass collection.

sites.name: Madison Historic District
sites.desc: An Ohio River town with one of the largest historic districts in the country.

sites.name: Lanier Mansion
sites.desc: Francis Costigan's 1844 Greek Revival mansion facing the Ohio River in Madison.

sites.name: Clifty Falls State Park
sites.desc: Waterfalls and a rugged canyon above the Ohio River near Madison.

sites.name: Falls of the Ohio State Park
sites.desc: Fossil beds of a 390 million year old coral reef exposed on the riverbank across from Louisville.
sites.wiki: Falls of the Ohio State Park

sites.name: Walker Art Center and Sculpture Garden
sites.desc: A leading museum of contemporary art, expanded by Herzog and de Meuron, beside the garden of Spoonbridge and Cherry.

sites.name: Minneapolis Institute of Art
sites.desc: A free encyclopedic museum with strong Asian, American and decorative arts collections in a McKim, Mead and White building.

sites.name: Weisman Art Museum
sites.desc: Frank Gehry's stainless steel museum (1993) on the river bluff of the University of Minnesota.

sites.name: Mill City Museum
sites.desc: Built in the ruins of the Washburn A Mill, telling how flour milling made Minneapolis.

sites.name: Guthrie Theater
sites.desc: Jean Nouvel's dark blue theater (2006) with its cantilevered Endless Bridge over the river.

sites.name: Stone Arch Bridge
sites.desc: James J. Hill's 1883 curved granite railroad bridge, now a walkway over St. Anthony Falls.

sites.name: American Swedish Institute
sites.desc: Swedish American culture in the 1908 Turnblad Mansion, a castle-like house with tile stoves.

sites.name: The Museum of Russian Art
sites.desc: A museum of Russian and Soviet-era art in a former church in south Minneapolis.

sites.name: Bell Museum
sites.desc: Minnesota's natural history museum and planetarium, known for its wildlife dioramas.

sites.name: Purcell-Cutts House
sites.desc: A 1913 Prairie School house by Purcell and Elmslie, owned by Mia and open for tours.

sites.name: Christ Church Lutheran
sites.desc: Eliel Saarinen's last major work (1949), with an education wing by Eero Saarinen.

sites.name: Foshay Tower
sites.desc: A 1929 obelisk skyscraper modeled on the Washington Monument, with a museum and observation deck.

sites.name: Minnehaha Falls
sites.desc: A 53 foot waterfall in a city park, made famous by Longfellow's Song of Hiawatha.

sites.name: Minnesota State Capitol
sites.desc: Cass Gilbert's marble capitol completed in 1905, with free tours.

sites.name: Cathedral of Saint Paul
sites.desc: Emmanuel Masqueray's Beaux-Arts cathedral with one of the largest domes in North America.

sites.name: James J. Hill House
sites.desc: The railroad baron's 1891 Richardsonian Romanesque mansion on Summit Avenue.

sites.name: Minnesota History Center
sites.desc: The Minnesota Historical Society's museum, with exhibits on the state's people, weather and industries.

sites.name: Science Museum of Minnesota
sites.desc: Large science museum on the Mississippi bluff in St. Paul, with dinosaurs and an omnitheater.

sites.name: Landmark Center
sites.desc: St. Paul's 1902 Romanesque federal courthouse with a soaring skylit court.

sites.name: Como Park Zoo and Conservatory
sites.desc: A free zoo and the 1915 Marjorie McNeely Conservatory glasshouse in St. Paul.

sites.name: Historic Fort Snelling
sites.desc: The 1820s stone fort above the meeting of the Mississippi and Minnesota rivers, interpreted with Dakota history.

sites.name: First Avenue
sites.desc: The Minneapolis club with its wall of stars, forever tied to Prince and Purple Rain.

sites.name: Paisley Park
sites.desc: Prince's home and recording complex in Chanhassen, open for tours.

sites.name: Minnesota Landscape Arboretum
sites.desc: The University of Minnesota's large arboretum in Chaska, with gardens, prairie and woodland drives.

sites.name: Franconia Sculpture Park
sites.desc: An open-air park of large contemporary sculpture in farm country, free and open year-round.

sites.name: Interstate State Park
sites.desc: Basalt cliffs and glacial potholes on the St. Croix River at Taylors Falls.

sites.name: National Farmers' Bank, Owatonna
sites.desc: Louis Sullivan's 1908 bank, the first and grandest of his jewel box banks, with ornament by George Elmslie.

sites.name: SPAM Museum
sites.desc: Hormel's free museum in Austin devoted to the famous canned meat.

sites.name: Plummer Building, Mayo Clinic
sites.desc: A 1928 tower with a carillon, the historic heart of the Mayo Clinic in Rochester.

sites.name: Mayowood
sites.desc: The country home of Charles H. Mayo outside Rochester, open for tours.

sites.name: Minnesota Marine Art Museum
sites.desc: Winona museum of art inspired by water, from Hudson River painters to Monet and Van Gogh.

sites.name: Niagara Cave
sites.desc: A show cave with an underground waterfall in Minnesota's bluff country.

sites.name: Pipestone National Monument
sites.desc: Quarries of red pipestone still worked by Native Americans, set in tallgrass prairie.

sites.name: Jeffers Petroglyphs
sites.desc: Thousands of carvings on a red quartzite outcrop in the prairie, sacred to the Dakota.

sites.name: Jolly Green Giant
sites.desc: A 55 foot statue of the vegetable mascot in Blue Earth.

sites.name: Saint John's Abbey Church
sites.desc: Marcel Breuer's concrete abbey church (1961) fronted by its great bell banner.

sites.name: Charles A. Lindbergh House
sites.desc: Boyhood farm of the aviator on the Mississippi at Little Falls.

sites.name: Sinclair Lewis Boyhood Home
sites.desc: Sauk Centre home of the author of Main Street, the first American to win the Nobel Prize in literature.

sites.name: Mille Lacs Indian Museum
sites.desc: Museum of the Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe, created with the band.
sites.wiki: Mille Lacs Indian Museum and Trading Post

sites.name: Itasca State Park
sites.desc: Minnesota's oldest state park, where you can walk across the headwaters of the Mississippi.

sites.name: Paul Bunyan and Babe the Blue Ox
sites.desc: The 1937 statues on the Bemidji lakeshore, among the most photographed roadside giants in America.
sites.wiki: Paul Bunyan and Babe the Blue Ox

sites.name: Glensheen
sites.desc: The Congdon family's 1908 estate on the Duluth shore, run by the University of Minnesota Duluth.

sites.name: Aerial Lift Bridge
sites.desc: Duluth's lift bridge over the ship canal, best seen when a lake freighter passes.

sites.name: Tweed Museum of Art
sites.desc: The University of Minnesota Duluth's art museum, free.

sites.name: Lake Superior Railroad Museum
sites.desc: Locomotives inside Duluth's 1892 Union Depot, with excursion trains along the North Shore.

sites.name: Split Rock Lighthouse
sites.desc: A 1910 lighthouse on a cliff above Lake Superior, run by the Minnesota Historical Society.

sites.name: Gooseberry Falls State Park
sites.desc: Waterfalls cascading toward Lake Superior, with CCC-era stone buildings.

sites.name: Tettegouche State Park
sites.desc: Cliffs, sea stacks and the High Falls of the Baptism River on the North Shore.

sites.name: Grand Portage National Monument
sites.desc: A reconstructed fur trade depot at the start of the 8.5 mile portage, with the Grand Portage Band of Lake Superior Chippewa.

sites.name: Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness
sites.desc: More than a million acres of lakes and portages in the Superior National Forest, best entered from Ely.

sites.name: International Wolf Center
sites.desc: Ely center with a resident wolf pack and exhibits on wolf ecology.

sites.name: Soudan Underground Mine
sites.desc: Ride a cage half a mile down into Minnesota's oldest iron mine.
sites.wiki: Lake Vermilion-Soudan Underground Mine State Park

sites.name: Hull-Rust-Mahoning Open Pit Iron Mine
sites.desc: An overlook into one of the largest open pit iron mines in the world, at Hibbing.

sites.name: Greyhound Bus Museum
sites.desc: Hibbing museum of the bus line that began here in 1914.

sites.name: Judy Garland Museum
sites.desc: Grand Rapids museum at Garland's restored childhood home.

sites.name: Voyageurs National Park
sites.desc: A water-based park of interconnected lakes on the Canadian border, explored by boat.

sites.name: Taliesin
sites.desc: Frank Lloyd Wright's home, studio and estate near Spring Green, part of the UNESCO listing of his work.

sites.name: House on the Rock
sites.desc: Alex Jordan's sprawling, eccentric house and collections, including the Infinity Room and a giant carousel.

sites.name: American Players Theatre
sites.desc: Classical theater performed in an outdoor hilltop amphitheater at Spring Green, June to October.

sites.name: A. D. German Warehouse
sites.desc: Wright's 1917 concrete warehouse in his birthplace of Richland Center, with a Mayan-style frieze.

sites.name: Mineral Point and Pendarvis
sites.desc: Stone cottages built by Cornish miners in the 1840s, now a state historic site in an arts town.

sites.name: New Glarus
sites.desc: A Swiss immigrant town with chalets, a Swiss museum village and a well-known brewery.

sites.name: Cave of the Mounds
sites.desc: A show cave of colorful formations near Blue Mounds.

sites.name: Dickeyville Grotto
sites.desc: Father Mathias Wernerus's 1920s shrines built of stone, glass and shells.

sites.name: Villa Louis
sites.desc: The Dousman family's Victorian estate at Prairie du Chien on the Mississippi.

sites.name: Wyalusing State Park
sites.desc: Bluffs 500 feet above the meeting of the Wisconsin and Mississippi rivers.

sites.name: Devil's Lake State Park
sites.desc: A lake below 500 foot quartzite bluffs in the Baraboo Hills, crossed by the Ice Age Trail.

sites.name: Circus World
sites.desc: At the Ringling Brothers' original winter quarters in Baraboo, with circus wagons and summer shows.

sites.name: Aldo Leopold Shack and Farm
sites.desc: The farm where Leopold wrote A Sand County Almanac. Visit the Leopold Center; Shack tours by reservation.

sites.name: Dr. Evermor's Forevertron
sites.desc: Tom Every's giant scrap-metal sculpture park near Baraboo.

sites.name: Seth Peterson Cottage
sites.desc: One of Wright's last designs, a tiny stone cottage in Mirror Lake State Park that can be rented or toured.

sites.name: Dells of the Wisconsin River
sites.desc: Sandstone gorges on the Wisconsin River, best seen by boat, beside the resort strip of Wisconsin Dells.

sites.name: Wisconsin State Capitol
sites.desc: George B. Post's granite-domed capitol (1917) at the center of Madison's isthmus. Free tours.

sites.name: Monona Terrace
sites.desc: Convention center on Lake Monona built in 1997 to a Wright design first proposed in 1938, with a rooftop garden.

sites.name: First Unitarian Society Meeting House
sites.desc: Wright's 1951 church with a prow-shaped roof, built in part by its congregation.

sites.name: Chazen Museum of Art
sites.desc: The University of Wisconsin's free art museum, one of the largest university collections in the country.

sites.name: Madison Museum of Contemporary Art
sites.desc: Free contemporary art museum in Cesar Pelli's Overture Center, with a rooftop sculpture garden.

sites.name: Wisconsin Historical Museum
sites.desc: The state history museum on the Capitol Square.

sites.name: Wisconsin Veterans Museum
sites.desc: Free museum of Wisconsin's soldiers from the Civil War to today, on the Capitol Square.

sites.name: Olbrich Botanical Gardens
sites.desc: Gardens on Lake Monona with a gilded Thai pavilion and a tropical conservatory.

sites.name: University of Wisconsin Arboretum
sites.desc: Where Aldo Leopold and others pioneered prairie restoration in the 1930s.

sites.name: Milwaukee Art Museum
sites.region: Milwaukee and the Lake Michigan shore
sites.desc: Santiago Calatrava's Quadracci Pavilion with its opening wings, attached to Eero Saarinen's 1957 War Memorial Center.

sites.name: Harley-Davidson Museum
sites.region: Milwaukee and the Lake Michigan shore
sites.desc: The motorcycle maker's museum in its hometown.

sites.name: Milwaukee Public Museum
sites.region: Milwaukee and the Lake Michigan shore
sites.desc: A natural and human history museum famous for its Streets of Old Milwaukee and walk-in dioramas.

sites.name: Discovery World
sites.region: Milwaukee and the Lake Michigan shore
sites.desc: Science and technology museum and aquarium on the lakefront.

sites.name: Grohmann Museum
sites.region: Milwaukee and the Lake Michigan shore
sites.desc: Milwaukee School of Engineering's collection of art about human work, with a rooftop sculpture garden.

sites.name: Haggerty Museum of Art
sites.region: Milwaukee and the Lake Michigan shore
sites.desc: Marquette University's free art museum.
sites.wiki: Patrick and Beatrice Haggerty Museum of Art

sites.name: Villa Terrace Decorative Arts Museum
sites.region: Milwaukee and the Lake Michigan shore
sites.desc: A 1920s Italian Renaissance style villa with terraced gardens down to Lake Michigan.

sites.name: Pabst Mansion
sites.region: Milwaukee and the Lake Michigan shore
sites.desc: The brewer's 1892 Flemish Renaissance Revival mansion.

sites.name: Lynden Sculpture Garden
sites.region: Milwaukee and the Lake Michigan shore
sites.desc: More than 50 sculptures across a 40 acre park and estate.

sites.name: Mitchell Park Domes
sites.region: Milwaukee and the Lake Michigan shore
sites.desc: Three beehive-shaped glass domes of the 1960s with desert, tropical and seasonal gardens.

sites.name: Burnham Block
sites.region: Milwaukee and the Lake Michigan shore
sites.desc: A row of Wright's American System-Built Homes, affordable prefab designs of 1915 to 1917, with tours.

sites.name: Annunciation Greek Orthodox Church
sites.region: Milwaukee and the Lake Michigan shore
sites.desc: One of Wright's last works, a domed saucer of a church completed in 1961.

sites.name: SC Johnson Administration Building and Research Tower
sites.region: Milwaukee and the Lake Michigan shore
sites.desc: Wright's 1939 office with its forest of dendriform columns and the 1950 Research Tower in Racine. Free tours by reservation.

sites.name: Wingspread
sites.region: Milwaukee and the Lake Michigan shore
sites.desc: The largest of Wright's Prairie houses (1939), built for Herbert F. Johnson at Wind Point.

sites.name: Racine Art Museum
sites.region: Milwaukee and the Lake Michigan shore
sites.desc: A museum devoted to contemporary craft, with one of the largest such collections in North America.

sites.name: Yerkes Observatory
sites.region: Milwaukee and the Lake Michigan shore
sites.desc: The 1897 observatory on Geneva Lake with the largest refracting telescope used for research, open for tours.

sites.name: Old World Wisconsin
sites.region: Milwaukee and the Lake Michigan shore
sites.desc: Open-air museum of farmhouses and buildings from Wisconsin's immigrant communities.

sites.name: Kettle Moraine State Forest
sites.region: Milwaukee and the Lake Michigan shore

sites.name: The Ridges Sanctuary

sites.name: Leigh Yawkey Woodson Art Museum

sites.name: Apostle Islands National Lakeshore
sites.desc: Twenty-one islands with sandstone sea caves and lighthouses, reached by boat from Bayfield.

sites.name: Gateway Arch National Park
sites.desc: Eero Saarinen's 630 foot stainless steel arch (1965), with a museum of westward expansion beneath it.

sites.name: Saint Louis Art Museum

sites.name: City Museum

sites.name: Missouri Botanical Garden

sites.name: Forest Park

sites.name: Missouri History Museum

sites.name: Wainwright Building

sites.name: Cathedral Basilica of Saint Louis
sites.desc: Home to one of the largest collections of mosaics in the world.

sites.name: Pulitzer Arts Foundation
sites.desc: Tadao Ando's concrete gallery (2001) with works by Richard Serra and Ellsworth Kelly. Free.

sites.name: Contemporary Art Museum St. Louis
sites.desc: Non-collecting contemporary art museum next to the Pulitzer, free.

sites.name: Mildred Lane Kemper Art Museum
sites.desc: Washington University's free art museum in a building by Fumihiko Maki.

sites.name: National Blues Museum
sites.desc: Interactive museum of the blues on Washington Avenue.

sites.name: Bellefontaine Cemetery
sites.desc: A rural cemetery and arboretum with Louis Sullivan's Wainwright Tomb.

sites.desc: The 1894 Romanesque terminal with its Grand Hall, now a hotel with an aquarium and a wheel.

sites.name: Anheuser-Busch Brewery

sites.name: Ted Drewes Frozen Custard

sites.name: Laumeier Sculpture Park

sites.name: Hermann

guides.title: Champaign-Urbana and East Central Illinois
guides.intro: Start at home: two free university museums, Allerton's gardens on the Sangamon and Kickapoo's river valley make easy half days. Bloomington and the Amish towns of Arthur and Arcola round out a Saturday.

guides.title: Springfield and Lincoln Country
guides.intro: A classic weekend. Spend one day on Lincoln (the Home, the Presidential Museum, the Old State Capitol and the Tomb) and the next on the Dana-Thomas House and New Salem, with a Route 66 lunch at the Cozy Dog.

guides.title: Wabash Valley
guides.intro: The closest serious hiking to Champaign: Turkey Run and Shades canyons, Parke County's covered bridges (festival in October) and the Swope in Terre Haute.

guides.title: Route 66 and the Illinois River
guides.intro: Follow old Route 66 north through Funks Grove and Pontiac to the Gemini Giant, then cut west to Starved Rock and Matthiessen for canyon hiking. Spring brings waterfalls, January brings eagles.

guides.title: Chicago
guides.intro: Chicago has its own guide with more than a hundred sites. Drive about 2 h 20 min, or take Amtrak from Champaign to Union Station in about 2 h 30 min and explore by L and bus.

guides.title: Indianapolis
guides.intro: An easy two hours east. Newfields and its 100 Acres park, the Eiteljorg and State Museum in White River State Park, the Speedway Museum and the monumental War Memorial Plaza.

guides.title: Columbus, Bloomington and Brown County
guides.intro: Modern architecture in Columbus in the morning (book the Miller House tour ahead), then fall color in Brown County and Indiana University's museums in Bloomington.

guides.title: St. Louis Metro
guides.intro: Plan at least two days. Forest Park alone holds the free art and history museums; add the Gateway Arch, the Wainwright Building, the Pulitzer and the City Museum, and drive to Cahokia Mounds on the Illinois side.

guides.title: Northern Illinois and Galena
guides.intro: A loop of modern architecture and river towns: Farnsworth House, Wright's Laurent House in Rockford, the John Deere and Reagan sites, then two nights in Galena for the bluffs and the Grant Home.

guides.title: Great River Road
guides.intro: The Mississippi bluffs between Nauvoo, Hannibal and Alton. Pair Elsah's stone village and Pere Marquette's lodge with Mark Twain's Hannibal across the river.

guides.title: Muncie and East Central Indiana
guides.intro: A quieter art trip: the David Owsley Museum and Minnetrista in Muncie, Richmond's art museum and jazz history, and the Levi Coffin House on the Underground Railroad.

guides.title: Northern Indiana
guides.intro: Dunes and cars. Combine Indiana Dunes with Notre Dame's new art museum and the Studebaker Museum in South Bend, or go east to Shipshewana and the Auburn Cord Duesenberg Museum.

guides.title: Southern Indiana
guides.intro: Hills, caves and utopias: New Harmony's Roofless Church and Atheneum, Lincoln's boyhood farm, the domed West Baden Springs Hotel and Spring Mill's pioneer village.

guides.title: Louisville and the Ohio River
guides.intro: Museum Row on Main Street, the Speed, Churchill Downs and Old Louisville's Victorian streets, with Madison and Clifty Falls upriver on the Indiana side.

guides.title: Milwaukee and the Lake Michigan shore
guides.intro: Calatrava's art museum, the Harley-Davidson Museum and the Domes in Milwaukee, then Wright's Johnson Wax buildings and Wingspread in Racine and the Kohler Arts Center in Sheboygan.

guides.title: Southern Illinois and the Lower Ohio
guides.intro: Sandstone country in the Shawnee National Forest, cypress swamps on the Cache River, then across the Ohio to Paducah's quilt museum and Land Between the Lakes. Best in October.

guides.title: Madison
guides.intro: A walkable capital between two lakes: the Capitol, Wright's Monona Terrace and Meeting House, the free Chazen and MMoCA, and the Arboretum where prairie restoration began.

guides.title: Eastern Ozarks and Ste. Genevieve
guides.intro: French colonial Ste. Genevieve, then granite and springs: Elephant Rocks, Johnson's Shut-Ins, Onondaga Cave and a float on the Current River.

guides.title: Missouri River and central Missouri
guides.intro: Wine towns and river bluffs: Hermann, a stretch of the Katy Trail by bike, Benton's mural in the Jefferson City capitol, the Churchill Museum in Fulton and historic Arrow Rock.

guides.title: Driftless and the Wisconsin River
guides.intro: The richest weekend in Wisconsin: Taliesin and the House on the Rock near Spring Green, a play at American Players Theatre, Devil's Lake, Baraboo's Circus World and Leopold's shack.

guides.title: Bluegrass and Bourbon Country
guides.intro: Horse farms, distilleries and Shakers: Lexington's Keeneland and Horse Park, Frankfort's capitol and Buffalo Trace, Bardstown, Lincoln's birthplace and a night at Shaker Village.

guides.title: Cave Country
guides.intro: Mammoth Cave deserves a full day of tours (book ahead); add the Corvette Museum and the boat ride at Lost River Cave in Bowling Green.

guides.title: Northeast Wisconsin and Door County
guides.intro: Oshkosh's aviation museum and Lambeau Field on the way to Door County's lighthouses, bluffs and dark skies. Horicon Marsh is spectacular during fall migration.

guides.title: Nashville and Middle Tennessee
guides.intro: The Country Music Hall of Fame, the Ryman and Studio B, the new National Museum of African American Music, the Parthenon and the Frist, with the Hermitage and Franklin nearby.

guides.title: West Tennessee
guides.intro: Shiloh battlefield and Pinson Mounds, Tina Turner's school in Brownsville and Alex Haley's Henning, with eagles at Reelfoot Lake in winter.

guides.title: Memphis
guides.intro: Music and civil rights: Graceland, Sun and Stax, Beale Street and the Peabody ducks, and the National Civil Rights Museum at the Lorraine Motel.

guides.title: Eastern Kentucky Mountains
guides.intro: Arches of the Red River Gorge and Natural Bridge, crafts in Berea, Cumberland Falls and the Wilderness Road at Cumberland Gap.

guides.title: Kansas City and northwest Missouri
guides.intro: The Nelson-Atkins and the WWI Museum, 18th and Vine for jazz and the Negro Leagues, Truman's Independence, and Disney's Marceline or St. Joseph on the way.

guides.title: Southwest Missouri Ozarks
guides.intro: Ha Ha Tonka's castle ruins, the Wonders of Wildlife museum in Springfield, Laura Ingalls Wilder's farm and the Carver and Truman birthplaces.

guides.title: Cumberland Plateau
guides.intro: Waterfall country: Fall Creek, Burgess and Cummins Falls, Sewanee's Gothic campus, Sergeant York's farm and the English utopia of Rugby by Big South Fork.

guides.title: Southern Minnesota
guides.intro: Sullivan's jewel box bank in Owatonna, the Mayo Clinic's Plummer Building, the Marine Art Museum in Winona and, farther west, the prairie sites of Pipestone and Jeffers.

guides.title: East Tennessee and the Smokies
guides.intro: Knoxville's museums and Sunsphere, Oak Ridge's Manhattan Project history, the Museum of Appalachia, and the Great Smoky Mountains with Cades Cove.

guides.title: Chattanooga
guides.intro: A compact river city: the Hunter Museum and Walnut Street Bridge, the Tennessee Aquarium, and Lookout Mountain's Incline, Ruby Falls and Point Park.

guides.title: Twin Cities
guides.intro: A long weekend at least: the Walker, Mia and Weisman, the riverfront from Mill City to the Stone Arch Bridge, Summit Avenue and the capitol in St. Paul, and Saarinen's Christ Church.

guides.title: Central Minnesota
guides.intro: Breuer's abbey church at Collegeville, Lindbergh's and Sinclair Lewis's boyhood homes and, at the end of the road, the Mississippi headwaters at Itasca.

guides.title: Lake Superior
guides.intro: Duluth's lift bridge and Glensheen, then the North Shore drive past Gooseberry, Split Rock and Tettegouche to Grand Portage. Add the Apostle Islands from Bayfield on the Wisconsin side.

guides.title: Northwoods
guides.intro: Canoe country and the Iron Range: Ely's Wolf Center and the Boundary Waters, the Soudan mine, Hibbing's open pit and Voyageurs on the border.
